term.title: insertion

definitions.text: A chemical reaction or transformation of the general type: $$\ce{X-Z + Y -> X-Y-Z}$$ in which the connecting atom or group $\ce{Y}$ replaces the bond joining the parts $\ce{X}$ and $\ce{Z}$ of the reactant $\ce{XZ}$. An example is the carbene insertion reaction:  The reverse of an insertion is called an extrusion.
sources: PAC, 1994, 66, 1077. 'Glossary of terms used in physical organic chemistry (IUPAC Recommendations 1994)' on page 1125 (https://doi.org/10.1351/pac199466051077)

definitions.text: A general term given to a reaction involving the transfer of a guest atom, ion or molecule into a host crystal lattice.
sources: PAC, 1994, 66, 577. 'Definitions of terms relating to phase transitions of the solid state (IUPAC Recommendations 1994)' on page 583 (https://doi.org/10.1351/pac199466030577)
